subject: Re: SummitAI guaranteed response floor — internal review
messages:
From: Aiden Park <aiden.park@summitai.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya.lin@summitai.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: guaranteed response floor for SummitAI enterprise pilot

Hi Grace + Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — SummitAI’s pilot team is ready to move to an early production pilot (internal search + recommendations) and they have a procurement-level ask before legal signs off. They want a documented, contractual "response floor" for inference that reads roughly as:

  - Monthly uptime >= 99.995%
  - p95 response time <= 50 ms for production traffic (expected steady-state 600–800 QPS, spiky to 1k QPS)

They understand some of this is aggressive and are open to a technical path (dedicated pool + warm KV cache + prefix caching). Procurement is asking for a timeline and whether Redwood can commit to operational runbook items (warm standby, pre-warm windows, dedicated capacity).

I'm attaching our short ask doc (summitai_sla_request.pdf). Can you confirm what we can offer today vs what will need product/engineering changes? Also need an ETA for any infra changes and if we should propose a staged commitment.

Respectfully,
Aiden Park
Head of Platform Engineering, SummitAI
Aiden.Park@summitai.com

Attachments: summitai_sla_request.pdf

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: guaranteed response floor for SummitAI enterprise pilot

Folks — forwarding Aiden's note. High-level asks: very tight p95 target (50ms) at ~1k QPS and a 99.995% uptime target. SummitAI is a strategic pilot; potential to expand across their product lines if we can meet a short ramp.

What I need from you:
- Product: what parts of the stack make this dependency (model variant selection, KV/prefix caching, batching settings)? Are there immediate knobs we can flip for a staged commitment?
- Engineering: feasibility + timeline for the dedicated/reserved pool proposal and any kernel/throughput optimizations we’d need for sustained sub-50ms p95.
- Sales (Karthik): preference on commercial staging, and whether we should propose a phased SLA (e.g., 70ms p95 for first 30 days, technical uplift to 50ms in 8 weeks).

Also tagging Laura since this will likely require an exec review for carve-outs and discounting.

Thanks — I’d like a short sync tomorrow 9am PT if possible.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: guaranteed response floor for SummitAI enterprise pilot

Thanks Grace — quick thoughts from GTM:

- SummitAI is a high-probability expansion opportunity. If we can stage this, we should.
- Commercial approach I prefer: offer a two-stage commitment. Stage 1 (pilot): committed p95 = 70ms + reserved capacity + explicit runbook (incident contacts, pre-warm windows). Stage 2 (full prod): target p95 = 50ms after engineering signal and a 60–90 day validation window; add financial remedy/credit if we miss the full-prod SLA.
- Recommend tying price to the reserved capacity commit and a modest initial discount for a 1-year committed term.

I can propose language to Aiden after product/eng gives feasibility and Diego gives ETA.

— Karthik
Principal Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: guaranteed response floor for SummitAI enterprise pilot

Appreciate the context. Short technical assessment:

- Current hosted offering (multitenant) can't reliably guarantee 50ms p95 at 1k QPS for all model classes without dedicated capacity + kernel/path optimizations.
- Path to 50ms p95: combine dedicated GPU pool, model quantization to 4-bit where quality is acceptable, aggressive KV/prefix caching, and an ops runbook for pre-warm behavior during expected large releases.
- Estimated work: 6–10 weeks of targeted infra + runtime tuning to reach sub-50ms p95 in our priority workloads, assuming we can test on a dedicated pool. Includes: benchmarking, kernel selection tweaks, and an extended soak test.
- Intermediate offering: we can stand up a reserved pool and enable priority routing + warmed caches today; expected p95 ~65–80ms depending on model size.

I attached a short operational runbook draft for the reserved pool (redwood_operational_runbook_v1.md) that describes warm-up windows, on-call rotations, and failover to compatible model variants.

If Product and Legal sign off on staged SLA language, Engineering can commit to a delivery wave to meet Stage 2 in ~8 weeks. We’ll need a clear acceptance test (synthetic traffic + sample prod traffic replay) and a rollback/fallback policy.

— Diego
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: redwood_operational_runbook_v1.md

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: guaranteed response floor for SummitAI enterprise pilot

Good thread — pragmatic path.

Decision: we approve a staged SLA carve-out for SummitAI under the following constraints:

1) Commercial stage: pilot SLA = p95 70ms + reserved capacity + documented runbook; full-prod SLA = p95 50ms conditional on engineering validation (target 8 weeks from reserved pool start).
2) Legal to draft a limited carve-out with explicit acceptance tests, service credits, and a terminate/exit clause if the upgrade cannot be achieved after the validation window.
3) CS/Ops to own the runbook and readiness gates; Engineering to provide the test harness and a go/no-go milestone.
4) Sales to propose a one-year committed capacity with a commercial uplift for priority capacity; discounts/cap credits should be scoped by Revenue Ops.

Grace — please get Legal and CS looped and share a short one-pager we can send to Aiden that contains the two-stage commitment, timeline (start-of-reserved-pool -> 8 weeks -> validation), and next steps. Karthik — coordinate the commercial terms and draft the initial proposal. Diego — estimate any additional infra cost (GPU hours) so we can bake that into pricing.

Happy to sign off on the approach once the one-pager and legal language are in draft.

— Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
